newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says last Soviet warheads leaving Belarus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says last Soviet warheads leaving Belarus.

text.p: The last Soviet-era nuclear warheads were to be gone from Belarus by the end of the day on Tuesday, U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said, but it was unclear whether all the missiles would go, too.
Burns said U.S. officials were checking on the status of the missiles.
"The warheads are on a train which is proceeding towards Russia," Burns said at a midday briefing. He said the train was expected to cross the Russian border "a couple of hours from now."
This was at odds with comments made to Reuters on Monday by a spokesman for Moscow's strategic missile command who said the warheads had already left Belarus.

Burns said U.S. officials had seen "contradictory statements" about the whereabouts of the warheads and the SS-25 missiles from the former Soviet arsenal, and were contacting the governments of Russia and Belarus to determine exactly what was happening to the missiles.
A ceremony marking the warhead transfer was set for Wednesday, Burns said.

The moves complete one of the major arms control tasks since the Cold War, concentrating on Russian territory the nuclear arsenal which was spread across four new independent states after the collapse of the Soviet Union. Nuclear weapons were previously transferred to Russia from Ukraine and Kazakhstan.

Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, at loggerheads with his own parliament and Russia over plans to extend his powers, once threatened to keep a final 18 SS-25 strategic missiles as a bargaining chip against NATO's plans to expand eastward. But on Sunday Lukashenko said he understood the last missiles would leave on Tuesday.
Washington took a dim view of Lukashenko's plans to expand his authority, notably a referendum which the State Department viewed with scepticism.
Burns said on Tuesday that no U.S. observers had monitored the vote because "frankly, we thought that this would be a sham from the beginning. And from all accounts, we believe it was."
